D4·64g2 — 2026-09-15
chose: The conformance suite (1.2) masks volatile bytes BY SHAPE instead of injecting a clock: a run-minted ulid becomes <ULID> only when its time part falls in the run's window, a run-minted ISO timestamp becomes <TS>, the two relative-age labels (Nm/Nh/Nd ago, ~Nh/~Nd since) become <AGO>, scratch paths become <ROOT>/<HOME>. Fixture bytes are never masked. Goldens are recorded from the TypeScript reference only, and only after the fixture horizon (newest fixture event + the 1 h cold-resume gap) so the presence of time-gated lines cannot flip. Everything else is pinned by building the child's environment from nothing but PATH (scratch HOME, git identity, XDG dirs, peer registry, update cache, LANG, TZ). Chosen under autonomy while the run owner's O6 ruling is outstanding; a SOFAR_NOW override can still be added later and would only shrink the mask list.
over: Adding a test-only SOFAR_NOW clock override (plus a ulid seed) to the hot path so goldens compare unmasked, or leaving time-dependent surfaces out of the suite.
because: Masking needs no hot-path code change in either implementation, keeps the shape of every volatile field asserted (a malformed ulid or timestamp still fails), and ulid randomness would defeat an unseeded clock override anyway. Leaving session-start's time-gated lines out would drop the surface the 10k cap and preface composition depend on.
